2.2 Composition  
SEComEnabler consists of five components such as SEComDevTool, SEComClient, SEComDriver, 
SEComCommon, SEComPlugIn. 
 
2.2.1 SEComDevTool.exe  
SECS message definition tool of SEComEnabler. This program makes a SMD File. 
 
2.2.2 SEComClient.exe  
Configuration tool for SEComDriver SECS parameters. This program makes a SEComINI.xml File. 
 
2.2.3 SEComDriver  
SEComEnabler’s SECSDriver. This communicates with another SECSDriver and sends/receives 
SECS Message. 
 
2.2.4 SEComCommon  
Utility component of SEComDriver. This provides various methods. 
 
2.2.5 SEComPlugIn  
Manage component of SEComDriver. Developer access SEComDriver through it.

3.1.6.4 Editing SECS Message Definitions.  
1) Defined SECS Message Format  
 
 
/square6 Message Header 
The message header consists of a description of the  message’s name and function, followed 
by a single line providing information in the following format: 
 
MessageName: Sn Fm Wait-Flag AutoReply-Flag Direction  
 
MessageName:  Message name. (ASCII format)  
Sn Fm:  Stream and Function numbers of the message.  
Wait-Flag:  The letter ‘W’ indicates that the message interpreter must wait f or a secondary 
message after sending this primary message.  
AutoReply-Flag:  If SECS message includes the string ‘<R>’, SEComDriver replies the 
secondary message automatically when the primary message is received.   
Direction:  Message transmission direction. This field can have three types.  
- H /barb2rightE : Host to equipment  
- H  E : Equipment to host  
- H /barb2rightE : Both direction  
  
/square6 Message Body 
SECSEditor displays the body of message definition using the SECS-II tree structure format 
used in the Book of SEMI Standard 1996, Equipment Software, and Volumn1.

3.3 SEComSimulator  
3.3.1 Concept  
SECS Equipment Communication Simulator (SEComSimulator) application allows you to exchange 
messages with an equipment. These messages are complied with the Semiconductor Equipment 
Communication Standard (SECS). SEComSimulator has several functions to send, receive, and 
create messages that comply with the SEMI standard and communicate across the SECS-I or HSMS 
links. 
 
3.3.2 Feature  
/square6 SEComSimulator is a .NET application. 
/square6 SEComSimulator can be used as a virtual Host or vi rtual Equipment.  
/square6 Auto Transaction is possible for Stress Test.  
/square6 Real time Transaction Monitoring is possible.  
/square6 It is possible to change SECS Message Structure an d DataItem values at runtime.  
/square6 SEComSimulator presents SECS Transaction Library. It can be used to edit Transaction 
Messages, create a custom SECS Transaction Message Library and so on.  
/square6 SECS-I and SECS-II Trasaction logs can be used for  analysis. Moreover, SECS-I Log can be 
converted to SECS-II Log and analyzed.

1) Feature  
/square6 A SECS message represents either a primary message  or a secondary message. Each 
SECS Transaction contains two SECS Messages, obtain ed from the primary and 
secondary properties of the SECS Transaction message.

2) SECS Header  
A SECS Header consists of an ASCII description of t he message’s name and function, 
followed by a single line providing information in the following format: 
 
Message Name: Sn Fm Wait-Flag AutoReply-Flag Direction NoLogging  
  
MessageName: ASCII message name.  
Sn Fm:  Stream and Function numbers of the SECS message.  
Wait-Flag:  The letter ‘W’ in this field indicates that SEComSimulator must w ait for a 
secondary message after sending this primary messag e. This also indicates that 
SEComSimulator replies the secondary message automa tically when this primary message 
has been received. 
AutoReply-Flag: The string ‘<R>’ in the SECS message header indicates AutoReply-Flag .  
But SEComSimulator discards this flag.  
Direction:  Message transmission direction. This field can have two values:  
H→E: Host to Equipment  
H←E: Equipment to Host  
NoLogging-Flag:  ‘<NL>’ string in the SECS message header indicates NoLogg ing-Flag.  But 
SEComSimulator discards this flag. 
  
3) SECS DataItem  
/square6 SEComSimulator displays the body of the message de finition using the SECS-II tree 
structure format used in the Book of SEMI Standard 1996, Equipment Software,  
Volume1.

/head2right Log Mode:  You can select the scale on which you want to save individual Log Files.  
/head2right Log Level:  You can choose a level for your Log Files.  
/head2right Log Backup:  You can choose for how many days, to want to keep the Log Files.  
For details see, Log Configuration section of 3.3.4.11. 1) Configure Connection  section.  
  
3.3.7 SECS Message Stress Test 
Stress Test can be used to send one Transaction message repeatedly for every given interval. This 
option is available in Settings menu.  
 
 
/square6 Enter a value greater than or equal to 500 for Int erval and click on Start  button. 
/square6 Now, select a Transaction message in the Transacti on Library pane and click ‘Send Primary 
Message’. Now, SEComSimulator will send the selected message repeatedly for every given 
interval. 
/square6 You can change the message dynamically, but after changing send message, you must click 
‘Send Primary Message’ again. 
/square6 When you click on Stop  button, Stress Test will be stopped.

available in the Library menu. 
 
 
/square6 The user can either copy SECS-I Log text and paste  in the SECS-I Log or get from a file by 
clicking on the Browse button. 
/square6 If you click on the Convert button, the SECS-I Log  text will be converted to SECS-II Log. 
/square6 If you click on the Load button, it will convert t he SECS-I Log to SECS-II Log. Subsequently it will 
be converted to SMD format and will be loaded in the Transaction Library Pane of the main 
window of SEComSimulator. 
/square6 More over, you can save the resultant SECS-II Log text to a file, by clicking on the Save button. 
/square6 Another interesting feature is that, you can find out the corresponding message in the other log 
pane by double clicking on the first line of the message you want to trace. For example, if you 
want to find out the corresponding SECS-II message for a given SECS-I message, in the SECS-I 
Log, double click on the first line of the message you want to trace. Then it displays the 
corresponding SECS-II message in a different color. Similarly, you can select a SECS-II message 
and find out the corresponding SECS-I message.
